prompt: Drive a traffic light as a tiny state machine: a switch expression picks the next colour, and a second one reports how long each colour lasts. Unknown or missing states must fall back safely to red.
explanation: A switch expression (case X -> value) returns a value directly, so each branch is one arrow instead of a case/break pair, and there is no fallthrough to forget. The default branch makes the machine total: every unknown colour maps to the safe state instead of falling off the end. Because switching on a null String throws a NullPointerException, the null check has to come before the switch.
hints: A switch expression looks like: return switch (current) { case "green" -> "yellow"; ... default -> "red"; };
Switching on a null String throws, so test for null with an if before you reach the switch.
secondsFor has the same shape but its arrows produce ints, and its default is 0.
